title: Adaptive capacity shaping for embeddings & rerank: throttles, preemptive failover, regional affinity
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Production reranker and embedding pipelines see intermittent tail latency spikes and capacity contention during bursty workloads from a small number of high-throughput customers. Existing regional routing and fallback rules are reactive and coarse-grained, causing avoidable throttling or broad downgrades that harm relevance.

Goal: Build an adaptive capacity shaping layer for the embeddings + rerank endpoint that throttles gently at ingress, preemptively migrates requests to alternative capacity tiers or regions when thresholds are predicted to be breached, and applies per-tenant regional affinity rules to reduce cross-region failovers. The system should prioritize high-SLA customers, preserve top-k quality for rerank, and reduce 95/99th percentile latency spikes by at least 30% under burst scenarios.

Scope:
- Implement an ingress throttling policy with progressive backpressure (token-bucket + dynamic rate adjustments) tied to observed queueing and GPU utilization.
- Add a predictive preemptive failover orchestrator that uses short-term telemetry (5s window) to trigger migration to alternative model variants or regions before SLOs are violated.
- Implement regional affinity heuristics: prefer local region unless projected cost/latency benefit justifies cross-region routing; allow per-customer override via config.
- Integrate a lightweight circuit breaker per-rerank shard that can trip to a degraded code path (smaller model, cached KV path) with automated recovery.

Non-goals:
- Full refactor of autoscaler or scheduler (this will be coordinated but not rewritten in this ticket).
- Changes to model architectures or training.

Constraints & risks:
- Prediction errors could cause unnecessary migrations, increasing cross-region cost.
- Per-tenant rules increase config surface; must ensure validation and safe defaults.
- Need to keep added latency from decision logic under 2ms median at ingress.

Success metrics:
- 95th/99th latency for rerank endpoint reduced by >=30% during simulated bursts (bench dashboard).
- Reduction in SLO breaches tied to capacity exhaustion by >=50% month-over-month for customers in pilot.
- Measured cost delta for pilot customers remains within +/-5% of baseline (target neutral or better).
acceptance_criteria: Ingress throttling implemented and enabled behind a feature flag in staging
Predictive preemptive failover triggers and logs decisions for at least two different simulated burst shapes
Regional affinity config available per-customer in Console controls and defaults to 'prefer-local'
Circuit breaker trips to degraded code path and recovers automatically; recovery behavior documented
Benchmarks show >=30% reduction in 95th/99th latency for rerank under 3 synthetic burst profiles
Integration test coverage for throttling+failover decision matrix added to CI
Runbook and post-mortem template updated; team runbook validated in tabletop exercise
tasks: Design decision doc: compare prediction models (EWMA vs light-weight ML) and select telemetry signals
Implement ingress token-bucket with dynamic rate adjustment (server side)
Build preemptive failover orchestrator service and proto for decision API
Add per-tenant regional affinity configuration in control plane and Console toggle
Create degraded rerank code path (quantized smaller model + KV-prefetch) and feature-flag it
Wire circuit breaker metrics and expose in Console and alerts
Write e2e bench harness for burst scenarios and update benchmarks dashboard
Deploy to canary subset of customers and run 2-week pilot, collect metrics
comments: 2025-02-11 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff - consolidated requirements from PM + SRE. Attached preliminary latency traces from 2025-02-03 incident. Action: prototype ingress throttling in sandbox.

2025-02-17 - Marco Chen: Design sync - decided to start with EWMA + GPU-utilization heuristic for predictive signal; we will revisit ML model after pilot. Agreed to keep decision logic <2ms. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ENG-51904-design
2025-02-20 - Riley Gomez (SRE): SRE review - flagged risk of double-throttling with existing edge quotas. Task: add de-duplication check between edge quota layer and new ingress throttle.

2025-02-24 - Marco Chen: Implementation update - token-bucket + dynamic scaler implemented in staging; feature-flag toggles present. Running microbench to validate decision latency (median 0.9ms). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/1427

2025-02-28 - Product (Sofia Martinez): PM review - requested a conservative default for regional affinity (prefer-local) and per-customer override. Also requested that rollouts start with non-enterprise SKUs to limit blast radius.

2025-03-03 - Marco Chen: Pilot prep - preemptive failover orchestrator can trigger simulated migrations; we logged decision traces and added event IDs for observability. Bench harness shows initial 22% reduction in p95; p99 still high. Next: enable degraded rerank path and tune preemption thresholds.
2025-03-04 - Aisha Patel: Stakeholder note - scheduled tabletop exercise for runbook on 2025-03-10 with SRE, PM, and Solutions Engineering to validate customer-facing behaviors and escalation paths.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: EWMA is simple and predictable but may underreact to very short spikes; ML model would be more accurate but expensive to maintain. Decided staged approach: EWMA first, ML after pilot.
Escalation policy: If pilot increases cross-region egress costs >10% for pilot customers, rollback to feature-flag off and open a cost review task.
Future follow-ups: integrate with Dedicated capacity pool API to respect reserved commitments, add per-route cost budget constraints
